- H1: separable epochs x FLOPs replaced by an accuracy-per-second curve.
- H1.1: the wide net is at the 75% edge at about 10 epochs under the E004 regularization.
- H1.2: only a mild width cut can pay.

- H3.2: judged on time at feasibility.
- H4: the <10% cap is dropped.
- H4.1: regularization strength depends on the epoch budget.

New Lvl1 K1: regularization x resolution x capacity jointly set the slope and the ceiling. It explains the committee counterexamples:
- E007/E009: capacity ceiling and a late-training width law (C0039). Tested by K1a1.
- E008: resolution as a FLOP lever plus a per-step remainder that does not scale with resolution (H3.2, K14).

1. Rerun E004 for the noise floor and feasibility (K2).
2. Resizing on E004 with extra epochs: 50% at 24 px at 11 ep (K6); 24/28/32 by thirds (K7).
3. Single-variable regularization tests at 10 ep: LS 0.05/0 (K9), translate 2 (K10).
4. Current-recipe slope, 10 to 9 ep (K3).
5. Then batch 512 (K12a), LR floor (K13a), fused optimizer in the graph (K14a), first-trial warmup (K14b), and a milder width cut 128/320/480 (K4).

updates.statement: Sample efficiency dominates time-to-75%. An airbench-style whitened CNN (frozen patch-whitening, dirac init, BN, Nesterov SGD, label smoothing, Lookahead) reaches 75% on CIFAR-100 in about 10 epochs: E004 took 8.94 s, against 59 s for the organizers' ResNet9. Within that family, the best time is set by the recipe's accuracy-per-second curve, and that curve cannot be split into epochs x FLOPs/epoch (E009).
updates.reason: The family hit feasibility at 8.94 s, about 6.6x faster than baseline, which supports the core claim. E009 contradicts the separable 'epochs x FLOPs/epoch' framing (narrow net plus more epochs fell short), so the statement is reworded.

updates.statement: The 128/384/576 airbench96-layout net, with regularization re-tuned for the short budget (E004: no cutout, LS 0.1), sits at the 75% edge at about 10 epochs without TTA. Its accuracy-vs-epochs curve is smooth near the edge, so the cheapest feasible epoch count for any change can be found by interpolating a measured slope.
updates.reason: Both original children fail as stated. The original claim, '8.5 epochs with airbench96 settings', is refuted: E001 reached 0.7304. A plausible cause is that the deleted futurebiohackers source used TTA. The reworded claim matches E004 (10 ep, 0.7550). The smooth-interpolation part is untested under the current recipe because the only slope (E001->E002) was measured under cutout + LS 0.2.
E001-: 0.7304, about 2.3 pp below 0.753. That is far outside the ~0.17 pp sd of a 3-seed mean. The noise-floor repeat in the same prediction was never run; it is moved to a new Lvl3 (rerun E004).

The crossing clause is false: at 10 ep the accuracy was still 0.7435 (E002) under the old recipe. The slope clause holds (0.87 pp/epoch, time ~0.9-1.0 s/epoch, intercept ~0). But it was measured only under cutout 12 + LS 0.2, and the E009 post-mortem shows slope depends on recipe and capacity. It must not be reused as the current-recipe slope; a new Lvl3 under H1.1 measures that.

updates.statement: Width/depth trade-off: a moderately cheaper net (stage-2/3 width or depth cut, while its capacity ceiling stays well above 0.753) trained for more epochs reaches 75% in less wall time than 128/384/576 at 10 epochs. A cut as deep as 128/256/384 is past that point: its ceiling at this recipe is about 75% (E009).
updates.reason: E009: 128/256/384 at 12 ep reached 0.7456 at 7.44 s, and +2 epochs bought only ~0.27 pp/epoch. Lit C0037/C0039 says width and steps do not trade at a fixed rate, and C0014 weakly favors width. A milder cut is still possible under C0038, so the claim is narrowed rather than dropped.

E007 is relabeled ~: it was infeasible, so it cannot support a claim about the best feasible configuration. E009 leans toward refuting: at the measured ~0.27 pp/epoch, 128/256/384 needs about 15 ep (~9.3 s), slower than E004. Not closed yet. It rests on a slope from two single runs (~2 sigma), and E007 may have run on an older base, which would confound the slope.

This is an understanding question: ablating whitening or dirac can only slow the recipe. The CIFAR-10 prior (arXiv 2404.00498) is already strong. The time-relevant part (BN-bias LR scaling, long-schedule constants) moves to a new H4 node.
It cannot lower time (review), so it is pruned to save budget.

At ~10 epochs the wide net under-fits: the airbench96 augmentation (cutout 12, translate 4) and label smoothing 0.2 over-regularize, and weaker augmentation and less smoothing improve accuracy at fixed epochs. Longer runs (e.g. resize plus extra epochs, >= 12 ep) may need some regularization back (lit C0040).
updates.reason: E004+: removing cutout and setting LS 0.1 gave +1.26 pp at 10 epochs (the E004/E005 descriptions say 8.5 ep, but timing and later rewrites show 10). Which of the two changes produced the gain is unknown. Translate and LS < 0.1 are untested; Fable's record uses translate 2 and LS 0.09. Kept open for those tests.
E004+: 0.7550 vs 0.7424 (E003) at equal epochs, +1.26 pp, about 5 sigma of a run-to-run difference. This is the only feasible run, so it depends on the pending E004 rerun for reproducibility.

E005 is down-weighted to ~. The -0.41 pp drop with random flip is about 1.7 sigma of a run-to-run difference: directionally supportive but not established. Alternating flip is free and stays in the recipe. No follow-up is needed, and its effect size should not be cited.

new.statement: Time-to-75% is set by the recipe's accuracy-per-FLOP curve. Regularization strength, resolution schedule and capacity together set both the per-epoch slope and the ceiling. The per-epoch slope is not a property of the short-budget regime; it shrinks as accuracy nears the architecture's ceiling under its current regularization. The cheapest feasible point therefore keeps capacity headroom well above 0.753, matches regularization to epoch count, and spends FLOPs on cheap low-resolution steps.
new.source: results (E004, E007, E008, E009); review (Lvl1 coverage); search: lit C0037, C0039, C0040; arxiv.org/html/2404.00498v2 (airbench96 CIFAR-100 ceiling ~79%)

new.statement: Capacity ceiling: under the E004 recipe, 128/256/384 saturates near 75-75.5%, so extra epochs return only ~0.3 pp/epoch. The 128/384/576 net has a long-schedule ceiling around 79% and returns ~0.8-0.9 pp/epoch near 10 epochs. Because the narrow-net deficit follows a late-training width^-c law (C0039), it grows with epochs instead of shrinking.
new.source: results (E007, E009 post-mortem); search: lit C0039; arxiv.org/html/2404.00498v2

new.statement: On the E004 base, the accuracy gap between 128/256/384 and 128/384/576 is at least 0.5 pp larger at 12 epochs than at 8 epochs, with both widths run at both epoch counts. If the gap stays flat or shrinks, the ceiling mechanism is refuted and E009's flat slope came from noise or a recipe confound.
new.source: review (H1.2.1 confound); search: lit C0039

new.statement: Noise floor: rerunning E004 unchanged gives a 3-seed-mean accuracy within +/-0.35 pp of 0.7550 that stays >= 0.753, and a mean time within +/-0.1 s of 8.94 s. The measured difference sets the 'within noise' threshold (about 2x the sd of a difference) for all later verdicts, and the per-seed minimum is logged.
new.source: review (noise floor; E004 as incumbent)

new.statement: Slope under the current recipe: cutting E004 from 10 to 9 epochs (schedule rescaled) lowers 3-seed accuracy by 0.5-1.0 pp and time by 0.8-1.0 s. In other words, the light-regularization wide net still gains >= 0.5 pp/epoch near 10 epochs.
new.source: review (slope assumption); results (E002, E004)

new.statement: A milder width cut, 128/320/480 (same 3-conv layout, ~0.77x conv FLOPs/epoch), on the E004 recipe at about 11 epochs reaches 3-seed accuracy >= 0.753 at a mean time <= 8.4 s.
new.source: search: lit C0038 (milder cut may still pay); results (E009)

new.statement: A 2-conv-per-block 128/384/576 net on the E004 recipe, at the epoch count whose time matches E004 (~8.9 s), scores 3-seed accuracy >= 0.753, i.e. at least as high as the 3-conv net at 10 epochs.
new.source: review (untried depth variants)

new.statement: The E008 resize schedule (first 50% of steps at 24 px) on the E004 recipe, extended to 11 epochs (schedule rescaled), reaches 3-seed accuracy >= 0.753 at a mean time <= 8.3 s.
new.source: results (E008); review (E008 follow-up top priority); search: lit C0024

new.statement: A 24/28/32 px curriculum by thirds of steps (bilinear downsample of the full augmented image, all shapes compiled and graphed in build) on the E004 recipe at 10.5-11 epochs reaches 3-seed accuracy >= 0.753 at a mean time <= 8.2 s. It loses less accuracy per second saved than the 50%-at-24 px schedule.
new.source: search: raw.githubusercontent.com/fulcrumresearch/cifar-10-speedrun/main/investigations/24px-curriculum.md; fulcrum.inc/2026/07/09/fable-cifar-speedrun.html

new.statement: At the E008 setting (10 ep, 50% of steps at 24 px), using antialiased (or area) downsampling and scaling translate to ~3 px during the low-res phase recovers >= 0.3 pp of E008's 0.55 pp loss at the same time cost. The mechanisms are aliasing mismatched to the frozen 32 px whitening filters, and translate that is effectively too strong at 24 px.
At 10 epochs on E004, lowering label smoothing from 0.1 to 0.05 (and separately to 0.0), changing nothing else, raises 3-seed accuracy by >= 0.3 pp for at least one of the two values.
new.source: review (H4.1.1 attribution); search: fulcrumresearch champion recipe (LS 0.09)

new.statement: At 10 epochs on E004, reducing translate from 4 px to 2 px (reflect padding), changing nothing else, raises 3-seed accuracy by >= 0.3 pp at equal time.
new.source: review; search: raw.githubusercontent.com/fulcrumresearch/cifar-10-speedrun/main/fable-100m/recipes/e1_1.74s_single-gpu_CHAMPION.py (translate 2)

new.statement: Regularization and budget interact. On a run of >= 12 effective epochs (e.g. a resize run extended for feasibility), adding cutout 8 back raises 3-seed accuracy by >= 0.3 pp, whereas at 10 epochs it lowers accuracy.
new.source: search: lit C0040; results (E004, E009)

new.statement: Batch size and steps: at ~10 epochs the run is limited by optimizer steps. A smaller batch (more steps per epoch at similar FLOPs) raises accuracy per epoch more than the lost GPU efficiency costs in time. Fable's CIFAR-10 record used batch 1536, which argues the other way.
new.source: review (untried batch size); results (E007 post-mortem); search: fulcrumresearch champion recipe (batch 1536)

new.statement: Batch 512 (lr scaled by the airbench convention) at 10 epochs on E004 raises 3-seed accuracy by >= 0.5 pp at a time cost <= +10%, which lets epochs be cut to below E004's time at accuracy >= 0.753.
new.source: review

new.statement: airbench96 schedule and optimizer constants tuned for 37 epochs (10% warmup, linear decay to 0, momentum 0.85, Lookahead cadence and alpha schedule, whiten_bias_epochs 3) are off-optimal at 10 epochs. bias_scaler 64 on BN biases must be confirmed present, since it is the largest sample-efficiency lever after whitening on CIFAR-10.
new.source: search: raw.githubusercontent.com/KellerJordan/cifar10-airbench/master/legacy/airbench96.py; arxiv.org/html/2404.00498v2 (bias scaling 18->13.5 ep); lit C0011-C0013

new.statement: At 10 epochs on E004, decaying the LR linearly to a floor of 5% of peak (instead of 0), changing nothing else, raises 3-seed accuracy by >= 0.3 pp at equal time.
new.source: search: fulcrumresearch champion recipe (LR floor 0.05 with EMA tail)

new.statement: Per-step work that does not scale with resolution (eager SGD + Lookahead updates, BN/elementwise kernels, augmentation, interpolate) is a sizable share of the ~19 ms step. That is why a 24 px step costs ~0.68x rather than ~0.56x of a 32 px step (E008). Fusing the optimizer into compiled foreach ops inside the captured graph cuts it.
new.source: results (E008 16% vs ~22% FLOP saving); review (H2 profiling); search: raw.githubusercontent.com/fulcrumresearch/cifar-10-speedrun/main/investigations/24px-curriculum.md

new.statement: Moving the SGD + Lookahead update into compiled torch._foreach_* ops inside the captured train-step graph (per-step LR from a precomputed GPU table) cuts E004's mean time by >= 4%, with |delta accuracy| < the measured noise floor.
new.source: search: fulcrumresearch champion recipe (whole-run CUDA graph, fused foreach optimizer)

new.statement: Warming the H2D transfer and allocation path in build on synthetic tensors of the real data shape removes the ~0.08 s first-trial prepare overhead. First-trial prepare then falls to <= 0.08 s, giving ~0.02-0.03 s off the 3-trial mean.
new.source: results (E006 side observation: 0.146 s vs 0.062-0.066 s prepare)

structured_output.summary:
Statuses brought up to date: H1.1.1, H1.1.2, H2.2, H2.2.1, H2.3 and H2.3.1 refuted. H4.1.1 supported (E004 gave +1.26 pp, about 5 sigma). H3.2.1 inconclusive: its accuracy threshold measured the wrong thing. H1.3, H1.3.1, H2.1 and H2.1.1 retired (understanding-only, already adopted, or false premise). H1.2.1 drops to 0.15 and stays open: E007 is relabeled ~ and E009 leans toward refuting it, but a possible older-base confound in E007 keeps it from being closed. E005 is down-weighted to ~ (about 1.7 sigma).

Reworded:
- H1: separable epochs x FLOPs replaced by an accuracy-per-second curve.
- H1.1: the wide net is at the 75% edge at about 10 epochs under the E004 regularization.
- H1.2: only a mild width cut can pay.
- H2 (now 0.3): narrowed to per-step work that does not scale with resolution.
- H3.2: judged on time at feasibility.
- H4: the <10% cap is dropped.
- H4.1: regularization strength depends on the epoch budget.

New Lvl1 K1: regularization x resolution x capacity jointly set the slope and the ceiling. It explains the committee counterexamples:
- E007/E009: capacity ceiling and a late-training width law (C0039). Tested by K1a1.
- E008: resolution as a FLOP lever plus a per-step remainder that does not scale with resolution (H3.2, K14).

New decisive tests, in priority order:
1. Rerun E004 for the noise floor and feasibility (K2).
2. Resizing on E004 with extra epochs: 50% at 24 px at 11 ep (K6); 24/28/32 by thirds (K7).
3. Single-variable regularization tests at 10 ep: LS 0.05/0 (K9), translate 2 (K10).
4. Current-recipe slope, 10 to 9 ep (K3).
5. Then batch 512 (K12a), LR floor (K13a), fused optimizer in the graph (K14a), first-trial warmup (K14b), and a milder width cut 128/320/480 (K4).

The E004/E005 descriptions say 8.5 epochs but the runs were 10. Use 10 as the baseline in every rewrite.
